title: Her mother's favouring of her sister Joyce
summary: Her mother always said Joyce was prettier and more talented, and Joyce later told her she had thought Marian had everything.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But this all, all of this . . .
This all ties in. It really does.
It all ties in, doesn’t it?
It’s all part of a . . . It’s a thread, the common thread to the entire family.
I guess it is, because you can see that my sister was a different . . .

She was a different kind of a person than me. Incidentally, I suppose this contributes to my character too. My mother always led me to believe that Joyce was more talented in every way than me, that Joyce was prettier, and Joyce was . . .
. . . this and that. It took me many a year to think, well maybe I’m not so bad after all.

Sometimes it’s unfortunate that even if a parent does favor one child to the other, it shouldn’t be that . . . at least obvious to the two parties involved, because both pick up on it, positive or negative, however it might be.

It’s so funny, because now my sister and I have had conversations, which by the way I’m hail and hearty and she’s in bed, can’t move without crutches [laughs], just in terrible shape, but we talk about . . . something I never knew. She said, “I thought you had everything. You were able to play, and you were able to draw and paint. It seemed like I didn’t do anything as well as you did it.” This was a revelation to me. I never had any idea of this.
